The `if` statement is one of the most fundamental aspects of programming, used to perform decision-making operations based on specific conditions. Here’s a basic overview of how an `if` statement works in Java: **1. Basic `if` Statement** The simplest form of an `if` statement executes a block of code only if a specified condition is true. ```java if (condition) { // Code to execute if the condition is true } ``` **Example:** ```java int number = 20; if (number > 10) { System.out.println("The number is greater than 10"); } ``` In this example, the output will be "The number is greater than 10" because the condition (`number > 10`) is true. **2. `if-else` Statement** An `if-else` statement provides a secondary path of execution when the `if` condition is false. ```java if (condition) { // Code to execute if the condition is true } else { // Code to execute if the condition is false } ``` **Example:** ```java int number = 5; if (number > 10) { System.out.println("The number is greater than 10"); } else { System.out.println("The number is 10 or less"); } ``` In this example, the output will be "The number is 10 or less" because the condition (`number > 10`) is false. **3. `if-else-if` Ladder** Sometimes, multiple conditions need to be evaluated in sequence. This can be accomplished with an `if-else-if` ladder. ```java if (condition1) { // Code to execute if condition1 is true } else if (condition2) { // Code to execute if condition2 is true } else { // Code to execute if all above conditions are false } ``` **Example:** ```java int number = 15; if (number > 20) { System.out.println("The number is greater than 20"); } else if (number > 10) { System.out.println("The number is greater than 10 but less than or equal to 20"); } else { System.out.println("The number is 10 or less"); } ``` In this example, the output will be "The number is greater than 10 but less than or equal to 20" because the second condition (`number > 10`) is true. These are the basics of using `if`, `if-else`, and `if-else-if` statements in Java. They are essential for controlling the flow of your programs based on different conditions. You can also nest these statements within one another to handle more complex logical conditions.
